content:
Talia Benson: @here Incident taxonomy v1 rollout is scheduled for next week (Mon 5/20).

What’s changing
- IncidentBot declaration + escalate flows will require taxonomy fields.
- Postmortems will require the same fields + remediation SLA tracking.
- Dashboards will start slicing incidents by category/owner/region/tier.

Rollout timeline
- Mon 5/20: IncidentBot fields available (feature flag on) + updated runbooks live
- Wed 5/22: Fields become *mandatory* for new incidents (Hosted + Dedicated). Private (where Redwood is primary operator) follows the same standard.
- Week of 5/27: start backfill of last 90 days (sampling + QA spot checks)

Required fields (during active response)
1) Incident Category (taxonomy v1)
2) Impacted Surface (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private / Console / Control plane)
3) Primary Owning Team (auto-suggested; can override)
4) Region
5) Customer tier (Self-serve / Dedicated / Enterprise)

If you’re unsure, pick the closest category and use contributing factors in the postmortem. Reclassification is expected once we know root cause.

Links (internal)
- Taxonomy spec (v1): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/incident-taxonomy-v1
- Incident categorization policy (process + timing): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/incident-categorization-policy
- IncidentBot runbook (fields + examples): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/incident-bot-taxonomy-fields
- Postmortem template update: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/postmortem-template-taxonomy

Support/CS notes
- Support will see the category + owner in the incident channel topic + status updates.
- Category → support playbook mapping is here: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/incident-category-support-playbook

Owners for rollout questions
- Process: @Rafael Mendes / @Sean Gallagher
- Tooling: @Devon Price
- Postmortem template: @Chloe Martin
- Dashboards/metadata: @Allison Grant

Thanks all — the goal is less paging ambiguity + faster handoffs. :white_check_mark:

Sean Gallagher: +1. This is a big step toward making MTTR reporting not a spreadsheet exercise. Please actually fill the fields on declare — we’ll be enforcing it starting 5/22.

Rafael Mendes: Reminder from the policy doc: category + owner should be set at declare time. If you truly can’t tell, use `Unknown (needs triage)` and update within 15 min. We’ll treat “Unknown forever” as a process gap.

Devon Price: Heads up on IncidentBot behavior:
- If you choose a category + impacted service, it’ll auto-suggest owning team + pager route.
- If the modal errors, run `/incident debug` in the channel and paste output in #eng-sre.

(also: we’re rolling out behind a flag Monday morning; if you want to test early, DM me)

Chloe Martin: Postmortem template is updated in #postmortems as of today. It’s mostly the same, just adds a small “Taxonomy + SLA” section + action item tracking for TTM/TTR.

Allison Grant: For observability folks: metadata is landing in the incident dataset as `incident_category`, `impacted_surface`, `owner_team`, `customer_tier`, `region`. Dashboards will follow after we’ve got ~2 weeks of clean data.

Dev Patel: From Support side: THANK YOU. This will help us stop ping-ponging between teams when customers escalate. Quick Q: will category/owner show up in the status page updates too, or just internal?

Jasmine Liu: @Dev Patel internal only for now. Customer-facing comms still use the standard incident language (impact + mitigation + next update). Category will help us pick the right messaging/playbook, but we’re not exposing taxonomy terms externally in v1.

Mina Haddad: For routing incidents specifically — does “routing overload” include the case where fleet is fine but policy is sending too much to a single pool/region?

Rafael Mendes: @Mina Haddad yes — if the proximate issue is routing/policy driving load imbalance, use routing overload. If the proximate issue is “we don’t have GPUs” / pools can’t scale, use capacity exhaustion/autoscaling. If in doubt, pick one and we’ll reclass in PM.

Irene Choi: +1 on that boundary. Also: please don’t put everything under “capacity” because it’s the easiest word 😅. If it’s a bad route / single AZ drain / config push, route/policy category helps us find it.

Aisha Bello: Re: remediation SLAs — we’re starting with targets by severity + category + tier (TTM/TTR). Not all categories have the same expectations.

If you’re IC: when you declare Sev1/Sev2, please @mention Support in the channel if tier = Enterprise/Dedicated so comms isn’t chasing context.

IncidentBot: System message: Taxonomy fields are now available in IncidentBot (rollout flag: ON for #announcements). Use `/incident declare` to see the updated modal.

Sean Gallagher: Also FYI: Security incidents stay under Security IR. We’re only sharing a couple metadata fields so reporting doesn’t break (surface/region/tier). Don’t try to shoehorn security events into this flow.

Dev Patel: Got it, internal-only makes sense. We’ll update our escalation macro to ask for category + owner if missing.

Talia Benson: Great questions. Please drop edge cases into #eng-sre or the working notes doc (linked from taxonomy spec). We’ll do a quick cleanup pass after the first week of usage and publish any clarifications.

(reactions: Sean Gallagher added :thumbsup: to Talia Benson’s message; Mina Haddad added :white_check_mark:; Devon Price added :robot_face:)
